concepts.why: The answer claims an int always starts at 0, but a local int has no default value, so the rule it uses is wrong in Java.
This matches the listed wrong rule that local variables get a default value on their own. After int x; the local x is unassigned, not 0.
The answer treats x as holding 0 even though nothing was assigned. That breaks the rule that a local variable must be assigned before it is read.
The answer does not mention Math.round.
